Federated Identity Management enables users registered with the Identity Provider within one domain to access services at a partner domain, without requiring them to also register with the identity provider in the second domain. Replacing bilateral agreements between identifiers with a network thereof provides scope to enable a large, scalable, decentralised network of users and services. What's your favourite peer-to-peer network? Distributed Hash Tables (DHT) are decentralised and distributed means of providing a lookup service that underlie peer-to-peer networking. Existing surveys of the security issues and proposed solutions do not cover the full range of DHT algorithms nor vulnerabilities. This project shall aim to contribute to the existing literature by identifying and addressing gaps in the security analysis of DHTs

Project Title: Enhancing Collision Avoidance in Industrial Robot Manipulators through Gaussian Mixture Model-Based Potential Fields
Project Description: This topic could focus on the development and implementation of an obstacle avoidance algorithm that combines Gaussian mixture models with potential fields (or other approaches) to improve collision avoidance capabilities in industrial robot manipulators. The research could delve into the technical details of the algorithm, its effectiveness, and real-world applications. The research could address issues related to dynamic obstacles, scalability, and the algorithm's ability to adapt to changing environments, making it suitable for industrial automation applications.

Project Title: Design and Implementation of an ESP32-S3-Based Multimodal AI Assistant for Voice and Visual Interaction
Project Description: This project will design and develop a low-cost multimodal AI assistant using the ESP32-S3, integrating voice interaction and computer vision capabilities. The prototype will combine an ESP32-S3 camera, INMP441 microphone, MAX98357A audio amplifier, speaker and TFT display with the XiaoZhi AI platform. Users will interact with the system through spoken commands, while the camera provides visual information about the surrounding environment. The project will investigate real-time voice processing, image capture, Wi-Fi communication and AI-assisted responses. Performance will be evaluated using response time, voice recognition reliability, visual recognition accuracy and overall usability, demonstrating the potential of embedded hardware for affordable edge-connected AI assistants.

Project Title: Design and Development of an AI-Powered Voice-Controlled Smart Home Robot
Project Description: This project will design and develop an interactive AI robot capable of controlling smart-home devices through natural-language voice commands. The system will integrate an ESP32/ESP32-S3, microphone, speaker, servo motors and relay-based IoT devices within a 3D-printed robotic platform. An AI voice assistant will interpret user commands and trigger actions such as switching lights or appliances on and off while enabling basic conversational interaction. The project will evaluate voice-command accuracy, response time, communication reliability and actuator performance. The resulting prototype will demonstrate the integration of AI, IoT, embedded systems and robotics for intelligent home automation.

Project Title: Development of an AI-Enabled Social Robot with Voice Interaction and Expressive Movement
Project Description: This project will develop a small AI-enabled social robot capable of responding to spoken instructions and producing physical movements such as dancing, turning and gesturing. An ESP32-S3 will provide connectivity and interface with an AI voice assistant, while servo motors will control the robot's movements. Different voice commands will be mapped to predefined behaviours, allowing users to interact naturally with the robot. The project will investigate human–robot interaction, voice-command recognition, movement coordination and system response time. Experiments will evaluate how accurately and reliably the robot converts spoken instructions into appropriate physical actions, providing a practical platform for studying low-cost interactive and educational robotics.

Project Title: Development of an AI-Powered Educational Robot for Children
Project Description: This project will design an interactive educational robot that uses artificial intelligence to engage children through voice-based learning activities. The robot will use an ESP32-S3, microphone, speaker, display and servo motors to communicate and perform expressive movements. Children could ask questions or participate in activities involving mathematics, science, spelling or general knowledge. The system will provide spoken responses and physical gestures to create an engaging learning experience. The project will evaluate response accuracy, interaction time, usability and children's engagement with the system. It combines generative AI, embedded systems, robotics and human–robot interaction within an educational application.

Project Title: Development of an AI Voice-Controlled Mobile Robot with Autonomous Obstacle Avoidance
Project Description: This project will develop a mobile robot that combines natural-language voice control with autonomous navigation capabilities. Users will issue spoken commands such as move forward, stop or navigate to a predefined location, while distance sensors will continuously monitor the surrounding environment. If an obstacle is detected, the robot will override unsafe movement commands and perform an appropriate avoidance action. An ESP32 or ESP32-S3 will interface with motors, sensors and AI voice services. The project will evaluate voice-command accuracy, obstacle-detection performance, navigation success rate and response time, demonstrating how AI interaction and autonomous robotic control can operate together within a single system.

Project Title: AI Voice-Controlled Assistive Robot for Elderly and Disabled Users
Project Description: This project will develop a voice-controlled assistive robot designed to help users interact with household devices using simple spoken commands. An ESP32-S3-based system will integrate a microphone, speaker, servo motors and IoT-enabled switches for controlling devices such as lights and fans. The AI assistant will interpret natural-language instructions and provide voice feedback confirming actions. The project will evaluate command-recognition accuracy, response time, system reliability and usability. Particular attention will be given to accessibility and safe operation. The prototype will demonstrate how low-cost AI, robotics and IoT technologies can support independent living and accessible smart-home interaction.

Project Title: Improving Task Efficiency Through Enhanced Human-Robot Collaboration.
Project Description: The demand for human-robot collaboration is increasing across sectors such as manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics, highlighting the growing need for ongoing enhancements in collaborative methods between humans and robots in these environments. This project proposes to develop and optimise human-robot collaboration algorithms within various settings/industries, with the aim of enhancing task efficiency and overall productivity.

Project Title: Robot Adaptability through Observational Learning: A Study in Human-Robot Interaction
Project Description: The project centers on the development of adaptive learning methods that enable robots to observe and learn from human behaviours. By mimicking human actions and responses, these robots can adapt to new tasks or changes in environmental conditions, enhancing their versatility and usefulness in various applications. The adaptive learning method involves the use of machine learning techniques to facilitate the robots' learning process.

Project Title: Accurate Real-Time Object Dimension Estimation Using Camera Calibration and Computer Vision
Project Description: This project addresses the problem of deriving reliable real-world object measurements from 2D camera images by proposing a Computer Vision–based approach that uses a known planar reference (A4 paper) to establish metric scale. By leveraging geometric transformations and image processing techniques, the project aims to reduce measurement uncertainty and improve accuracy without requiring specialised hardware such as depth sensors or stereo camera systems.

Project Title: Machine Learning–Driven Waste Classification Using Computer Vision and Interactive GUI
Project Description: This project addresses the problem of automating waste classification using low-cost Computer Vision and machine learning techniques. The proposed system focuses on classifying waste items into four predefined categories, covering eight distinct waste objects, using image-based recognition. By leveraging supervised learning and visual features, the system aims to demonstrate how common waste items can be reliably identified and categorised using a standard camera and trained classification model.

Project Title: Development of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Chatbot for University Student Support
Project Description: This project will develop an AI chatbot that uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to answer questions from a controlled collection of university documents. Documents such as module guides, regulations and student-support information will be converted into embeddings and stored in a vector database. When a user asks a question, relevant information will be retrieved and supplied to a Large Language Model to generate a response. The project will evaluate response accuracy, retrieval quality, hallucination and response time. The study will demonstrate how RAG can improve the reliability of LLM-based applications by grounding responses in domain-specific information.

Project Title: Design of an AI Agent for Automated Business Workflow Management
Project Description: This project will design an AI agent capable of completing a multi-stage business task with limited human intervention. The system could process customer enquiries, classify requests, retrieve relevant information, generate responses and update business records using APIs and automation tools. The project will investigate how LLMs can reason over tasks and interact with external tools. Performance will be evaluated using task-completion accuracy, execution time, reliability and human intervention requirements. Particular attention will be given to situations where the agent makes incorrect decisions or fails to use tools appropriately, providing insight into the practical limitations of agentic AI systems.

Project Title: AI Audit Framework for Detecting Bias, Hallucination and Reliability Issues in LLM Applications
Project Description: This project will develop and evaluate a practical auditing framework for applications powered by Large Language Models. The framework will assess factors such as factual accuracy, hallucination, consistency, bias, transparency and robustness. A collection of structured test prompts will be created and used to examine how an LLM behaves across different scenarios. Automated metrics may be combined with human evaluation to assess system performance. The project will investigate whether systematic AI auditing can identify weaknesses before an AI application is deployed. The resulting framework could provide organisations with a repeatable approach for evaluating the reliability and responsible use of generative AI systems.

Project Title: Comparative Analysis of Prompt Engineering and RAG for Improving LLM Response Accuracy
Project Description: This project will investigate two approaches for improving the quality of Large Language Model responses: prompt engineering and Retrieval-Augmented Generation. A controlled question-answering application will be developed, and the same set of questions will be tested using a baseline LLM, engineered prompts and a RAG-based system. Responses will be evaluated for factual accuracy, relevance, hallucination, completeness and response time. The results will help determine the strengths and limitations of each approach for domain-specific applications. The project provides practical experience with LLM APIs, embeddings, vector databases, prompt design and systematic evaluation of generative AI systems.

Project Title: Development of a Multi-Agent AI System for Automated Task Coordination
Project Description: This project will investigate whether multiple specialised AI agents can collaborate to complete a complex task more effectively than a single AI agent. The proposed system could contain separate agents responsible for planning, information retrieval, analysis, content generation and verification. A coordinating mechanism will manage communication and task allocation between the agents. The system will be tested using predefined tasks and evaluated based on completion accuracy, execution time, number of errors, computational cost and human intervention. The project will explore the potential benefits and limitations of multi-agent architectures and provide practical insight into the development of more sophisticated agentic AI applications.

Project Title: AI-Based Smart Attendance System Using Facial Recognition
Project Description: This project will develop an intelligent attendance system that uses computer vision and facial recognition to identify students and automatically record attendance. A camera will capture images, while an AI model detects and recognises registered users. Attendance records can be stored in a database and displayed through a simple dashboard. The project will investigate recognition accuracy under different lighting conditions, distances and facial orientations. It will also consider privacy, security and ethical issues associated with biometric data. The final system should demonstrate how AI can reduce manual attendance processes while providing reliable attendance records.

Project Title: Development of an Intelligent Document Analysis and Information Extraction System
Project Description: This project will develop an AI application capable of extracting useful information from documents such as application forms, invoices, reports or academic documents. The system will process uploaded documents, identify important information and convert it into structured data for further use. Large Language Models or other natural language processing techniques can be incorporated to understand document content. The system will be evaluated using extraction accuracy, processing time and consistency across different document formats. The project will demonstrate how AI can automate document-heavy administrative processes and investigate challenges including missing information, inconsistent document structures, privacy and incorrect AI-generated interpretations.

Project Title: Development of a Human-in-the-Loop AI Automation Framework for Business Processes
Project Description: This project will develop an AI automation system in which important decisions are reviewed by humans before actions are executed. The system will classify tasks according to confidence or risk, automatically complete low-risk activities and escalate uncertain or sensitive decisions for human approval. A prototype could be demonstrated using customer enquiries, document processing or administrative workflows. The project will compare fully automated and human-in-the-loop approaches using accuracy, processing time, error rates and human intervention frequency. The research will demonstrate how organisations can benefit from AI automation while retaining appropriate human control over decisions that may have significant consequences.

Project Title: Inclusive Cybersecurity Awareness Education in Higher Education
Project Description: Explore how cybersecurity awareness education can better accommodate diverse university student populations. The project may consider accessibility, digital confidence, disciplinary background, prior cybersecurity knowledge and different learning needs, resulting in recommendations for inclusive cybersecurity awareness design.

Project Title: Design and Development of Gamification for Cyber education
Project Description: Design, implement and evaluate an interactive game that teaches university students how to recognise and respond to phishing attacks. The system could include email, messaging, QR-code and AI-assisted phishing scenarios, decision-making activities, feedback and progression mechanisms.

The research evaluates the feasibility, accuracy, and limitations of a lightweight vision-based waste classifier, with potential applications in smart bins, recycling facilities, environmental monitoring, and assistive decision-support tools.

Project Title: Social Media Behaviour Analysis Using AI
Project Description: Analysing social media content to identify behavioural patterns, public trends, or opinion shifts around a selected topic. The project may include sentiment analysis, clustering, trend detection, or visual analytics.

An AI-driven decision support system designed to assist in making predictions or recommendations in domains such as healthcare, education, business, or cybersecurity. The project focuses on predictive performance and on providing transparent explanations of how decisions are generated.

Project Title: Intelligent Text Classification and Content Moderation
Project Description: Automatically classifies, filters, or flags textual content such as emails, reviews, comments, or online posts. The project can explore different machine learning or deep learning approaches for tasks such as topic classification, harmful content detection, or risk assessment.
